title: SARATHI: Efficient LLM Inference by Piggybacking Decodes with Chunked Prefills
technique: chunked prefills + decode-maximal batching (decodes piggyback on a prefill chunk); uniform micro-batches reduce pipeline bubbles

optimized_metrics.evidence: For the LLaMA-13B model on A6000 GPU, SARATHI improves decode throughput by up to 10×, and accelerates end-to-end throughput by up to 1.33×.
the decode phase results in low compute utilization as it generates one token at a time per request ... the prefill chunk saturates GPU compute, while the decode requests 'piggyback'
SARATHI reduces the median bubble time per request by 6.29×, by creating equal-compute units of work.

headline_claim.text: For LLaMA-13B on A6000, SARATHI improves decode throughput by up to 10x and end-to-end throughput by up to 1.33x; LLaMA-33B on A100 1.25x end-to-end; GPT-3 pipeline bubbles reduced 6.29x, end-to-end throughput 1.91x

metric_definitions.definition_quote: decode phase throughput that we calculate based on the average time spent on decoding one token. For the baseline system, we compute the average decode time per token by dividing the time to process one decode iteration by the batch size.
metric_definitions.notes: per-token decode cost inverse, not request throughput

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We define this as the sum of bubble time for all the micro-batches across all iterations for a given request.

load_regime: offline batch / fixed batch size; sweeps over P:D ratio, sequence length, batch size; simulated 10K-request completion for GPT-3 pipeline
tradeoff_acknowledged: chunking overhead on prefill (smaller chunk lowers prefill efficiency, repeated KV loads); paper notes latency, queuing delays and fairness as unexamined dimensions
hardware: A6000 (LLaMA-13B), A100 (LLaMA-33B), simulated 64 A100 DGX for GPT-3
workloads: synthetic sequences with varied P:D ratios
extractor_notes: Throughput-oriented offline paper; no tail-latency metric, no SLO. Throughput units are tokens/ms (per-GPU single-layer plots) and normalized end-to-end throughput; chunk size picked to maximize throughput.
